personalbar.comment: Returns true if the personal bar is visible; otherwise, returns false.

scrollbars.name: scrollbars
scrollbars.comment: Returns true if the scrollbars are visible; otherwise, returns false.

statusbar.name: statusbar
statusbar.comment: Returns true if the status bar is visible; otherwise, returns false.

toolbar.name: toolbar
toolbar.comment: Returns true if the toolbar is visible; otherwise, returns false.

closed.name: closed
closed.comment: Returns true if the window has been closed, false otherwise.

parent.name: parent
parent.comment:
Refers to either the parent WindowProxy, or itself.

It can rarely be null e.g. for contentWindow of an iframe that is already removed from the parent.

clientInformation.name: clientInformation
clientInformation.deprecated: This is a legacy alias of `navigator`.

pageXOffset.name: pageXOffset
pageXOffset.deprecated: This is a legacy alias of `scrollX`.

pageYOffset.name: pageYOffset
pageYOffset.deprecated: This is a legacy alias of `scrollY`.

Window.comment: A window containing a DOM document; the document property points to the DOM document loaded in that window.

Location.name: Location

replace.name: replace
replace.comment: Removes the current page from the session history and navigates to the given URL.

href.name: href
href.comment:
Returns the Location object's URL.

Can be set, to navigate to the given URL.

origin.name: origin
origin.comment: Returns the Location object's URL's origin.

protocol.name: protocol
protocol.comment:
Returns the Location object's URL's scheme.

Can be set, to navigate to the same URL with a changed scheme.

host.name: host
host.comment:
Returns the Location object's URL's host and port (if different from the default port for the scheme).

Can be set, to navigate to the same URL with a changed host and port.

hostname.name: hostname
hostname.comment:
Returns the Location object's URL's host.

Can be set, to navigate to the same URL with a changed host.

port.name: port
port.comment:
Returns the Location object's URL's port.

Can be set, to navigate to the same URL with a changed port.

pathname.name: pathname
pathname.comment:
Returns the Location object's URL's path.

Can be set, to navigate to the same URL with a changed path.

search.name: search
search.comment:
Returns the Location object's URL's query (includes leading "?" if non-empty).

Can be set, to navigate to the same URL with a changed query (ignores leading "?").

hash.name: hash
hash.comment:
Returns the Location object's URL's fragment (includes leading "#" if non-empty).

Can be set, to navigate to the same URL with a changed fragment (ignores leading "#").

ancestorOrigins.name: ancestorOrigins
ancestorOrigins.comment: Returns a DOMStringList object listing the origins of the ancestor browsing contexts, from the parent browsing context to the top-level browsing context.

Location.comment: The location (URL) of the object it is linked to. Changes done on it are reflected on the object it relates to. Both the Document and Window interface have such a linked Location, accessible via Document.location and Window.location respectively.

History.name: History
History.comment: Allows manipulation of the browser session history, that is the pages visited in the tab or frame that the current page is loaded in.

PopStateEvent.name: PopStateEvent

state.name: state
state.comment: Returns a copy of the information that was provided to pushState() or replaceState().

PopStateEvent.comment: PopStateEvent is an event handler for the popstate event on the window.

HashChangeEvent.name: HashChangeEvent

oldURL.name: oldURL
oldURL.comment: Returns the URL of the session history entry that was previously current.

newURL.name: newURL
newURL.comment: Returns the URL of the session history entry that is now current.

HashChangeEvent.comment: Events that fire when the fragment identifier of the URL has changed.

PageTransitionEvent.name: PageTransitionEvent

persisted.name: persisted
persisted.comment:
For the pageshow event, returns false if the page is newly being loaded (and the load event will fire). Otherwise, returns true.

For the pagehide event, returns false if the page is going away for the last time. Otherwise, returns true, meaning that (if nothing conspires to make the page unsalvageable) the page might be reused if the user navigates back to this page.

Things that can cause the page to be unsalvageable include:

The user agent decided to not keep the Document alive in a session history entry after unload
Having iframes that are not salvageable
Active WebSocket objects
Aborting a Document

PageTransitionEvent.comment: The PageTransitionEvent is fired when a document is being loaded or unloaded.

BeforeUnloadEvent.name: BeforeUnloadEvent
BeforeUnloadEvent.comment: The beforeunload event is fired when the window, the document and its resources are about to be unloaded.

ErrorEvent.name: ErrorEvent
ErrorEvent.comment: Events providing information related to errors in scripts or in files.

DOMParser.name: DOMParser

parseFromString.name: parseFromString
parseFromString.comment:
Parses string using either the HTML or XML parser, according to type, and returns the resulting Document. type can be "text/html" (which will invoke the HTML parser), or any of "text/xml", "application/xml", "application/xhtml+xml", or "image/svg+xml" (which will invoke the XML parser).

For the XML parser, if string cannot be parsed, then the returned Document will contain elements describing the resulting error.

Note that script elements are not evaluated during parsing, and the resulting document's encoding will always be UTF-8.

Values other than the above for type will cause a TypeError exception to be thrown.

DOMParser.comment: Provides the ability to parse XML or HTML source code from a string into a DOM Document.

Navigator.name: Navigator
Navigator.comment: The state and the identity of the user agent. It allows scripts to query it and to register themselves to carry on some activities.

PluginArray.name: PluginArray
PluginArray.comment: Used to store a list of Plugin objects describing the available plugins; it's returned by the window.navigator.plugins property. The PluginArray is not a JavaScript array, but has the length property and supports accessing individual items using bracket notation (plugins[2]), as well as via item(index) and namedItem("name") methods.

MimeTypeArray.name: MimeTypeArray
MimeTypeArray.comment: Returns an array of MimeType instances, each of which contains information about a supported browser plugins. This object is returned by NavigatorPlugins.mimeTypes.

Plugin.name: Plugin

filename.name: filename
filename.comment: Returns the plugin library's filename, if applicable on the current platform.

length.name: length
length.comment: Returns the number of MIME types, represented by MimeType objects, supported by the plugin.

Plugin.comment: Provides information about a browser plugin.

MimeType.name: MimeType

suffixes.name: suffixes
suffixes.comment: Returns the MIME type's typical file extensions, in a comma-separated list.

enabledPlugin.name: enabledPlugin
enabledPlugin.comment: Returns the Plugin object that implements this MIME type.

MimeType.comment: Provides contains information about a MIME type associated with a particular plugin. NavigatorPlugins.mimeTypes returns an array of this object.

width.name: width
width.comment: Returns the intrinsic width of the image, in CSS pixels.

height.name: height
height.comment: Returns the intrinsic height of the image, in CSS pixels.

MessageEvent.name: MessageEvent

data.name: data
data.comment: Returns the data of the message.

origin.name: origin
origin.comment: Returns the origin of the message, for server-sent events and cross-document messaging.

lastEventId.name: lastEventId
lastEventId.comment: Returns the last event ID string, for server-sent events.

source.name: source
source.comment: Returns the WindowProxy of the source window, for cross-document messaging, and the MessagePort being attached, in the connect event fired at SharedWorkerGlobalScope objects.

ports.name: ports
ports.comment: Returns the MessagePort array sent with the message, for cross-document messaging and channel messaging.

MessageEvent.comment: A message received by a target object.

close.name: close
close.comment: Aborts any instances of the fetch algorithm started for this EventSource object, and sets the readyState attribute to CLOSED.

url.name: url
url.comment: Returns the URL providing the event stream.

withCredentials.name: withCredentials
withCredentials.comment: Returns true if the credentials mode for connection requests to the URL providing the event stream is set to "include", and false otherwise.

readyState.name: readyState
readyState.comment: Returns the state of this EventSource object's connection. It can have the values described below.

MessageChannel.name: MessageChannel
MessageChannel.comment: This Channel Messaging API interface allows us to create a new message channel and send data through it via its two MessagePort properties.

MessagePort.name: MessagePort

postMessage.name: postMessage
postMessage.comment:
Posts a message through the channel. Objects listed in transfer are transferred, not just cloned, meaning that they are no longer usable on the sending side.

Throws a "DataCloneError" DOMException if transfer contains duplicate objects or port, or if message could not be cloned.

start.name: start
start.comment: Begins dispatching messages received on the port.

close.name: close
close.comment: Disconnects the port, so that it is no longer active.

MessagePort.comment: This Channel Messaging API interface represents one of the two ports of a MessageChannel, allowing messages to be sent from one port and listening out for them arriving at the other.

postMessage.name: postMessage
postMessage.comment: Sends the given message to other BroadcastChannel objects set up for this channel. Messages can be structured objects, e.g. nested objects and arrays.

close.name: close
close.comment: Closes the BroadcastChannel object, opening it up to garbage collection.

name.name: name
name.comment: Returns the channel name (as passed to the constructor).

Worker.name: Worker

postMessage.name: postMessage
postMessage.comment: Clones message and transmits it to worker's global environment. transfer can be passed as a list of objects that are to be transferred rather than cloned.

Worker.comment: This Web Workers API interface represents a background task that can be easily created and can send messages back to its creator. Creating a worker is as simple as calling the Worker() constructor and specifying a script to be run in the worker thread.

port.name: port
port.comment: Returns sharedWorker's MessagePort object which can be used to communicate with the global environment.

addModule.name: addModule
addModule.comment:
Loads and executes the module script given by moduleURL into all of worklet's global scopes. It can also create additional global scopes as part of this process, depending on the worklet type. The returned promise will fulfill once the script has been successfully loaded and run in all global scopes.

The credentials option can be set to a credentials mode to modify the script-fetching process. It defaults to "same-origin".

Any failures in fetching the script or its dependencies will cause the returned promise to be rejected with an "AbortError" DOMException. Any errors in parsing the script or its dependencies will cause the returned promise to be rejected with the exception generated during parsing.

Storage.name: Storage

key.name: key
key.comment: Returns the name of the nth key, or null if n is greater than or equal to the number of key/value pairs.

getItem.name: getItem
getItem.comment: Returns the current value associated with the given key, or null if the given key does not exist.

setItem.name: setItem
setItem.comment:
Sets the value of the pair identified by key to value, creating a new key/value pair if none existed for key previously.

Throws a "QuotaExceededError" DOMException exception if the new value couldn't be set. (Setting could fail if, e.g., the user has disabled storage for the site, or if the quota has been exceeded.)

Dispatches a storage event on Window objects holding an equivalent Storage object.

removeItem.name: removeItem
removeItem.comment:
Removes the key/value pair with the given key, if a key/value pair with the given key exists.

Dispatches a storage event on Window objects holding an equivalent Storage object.

clear.name: clear
clear.comment:
Removes all key/value pairs, if there are any.

Dispatches a storage event on Window objects holding an equivalent Storage object.

length.name: length
length.comment: Returns the number of key/value pairs.

Storage.comment: This Web Storage API interface provides access to a particular domain's session or local storage. It allows, for example, the addition, modification, or deletion of stored data items.

StorageEvent.name: StorageEvent

key.name: key
key.comment: Returns the key of the storage item being changed.

oldValue.name: oldValue
oldValue.comment: Returns the old value of the key of the storage item whose value is being changed.

newValue.name: newValue
newValue.comment: Returns the new value of the key of the storage item whose value is being changed.

url.name: url
url.comment: Returns the URL of the document whose storage item changed.

storageArea.name: storageArea
storageArea.comment: Returns the Storage object that was affected.

StorageEvent.comment: A StorageEvent is sent to a window when a storage area it has access to is changed within the context of another document.

HTMLFrameSetElement.name: HTMLFrameSetElement

cols.name: cols
cols.comment: Sets or retrieves the frame widths of the object.

rows.name: rows
rows.comment: Sets or retrieves the frame heights of the object.

HTMLFrameSetElement.comment: Provides special properties (beyond those of the regular HTMLElement interface they also inherit) for manipulating <frameset> elements.

name.name: name
name.comment: Sets or retrieves the frame name.

scrolling.name: scrolling
scrolling.comment: Sets or retrieves whether the frame can be scrolled.

src.name: src
src.comment: Sets or retrieves a URL to be loaded by the object.

frameBorder.name: frameBorder
frameBorder.comment: Sets or retrieves whether to display a border for the frame.

longDesc.name: longDesc
longDesc.comment: Sets or retrieves a URI to a long description of the object.

noResize.name: noResize
noResize.comment: Sets or retrieves whether the user can resize the frame.

contentDocument.name: contentDocument
contentDocument.comment: Retrieves the document object of the page or frame.

contentWindow.name: contentWindow
contentWindow.comment: Retrieves the object of the specified.

marginHeight.name: marginHeight
marginHeight.comment: Sets or retrieves the top and bottom margin heights before displaying the text in a frame.

marginWidth.name: marginWidth
marginWidth.comment: Sets or retrieves the left and right margin widths before displaying the text in a frame.

HTMLFontElement.name: HTMLFontElement

face.name: face
face.comment: Sets or retrieves the current typeface family.

HTMLFontElement.comment: Implements the document object model (DOM) representation of the font element. The HTML Font Element <font> defines the font size, font face and color of text.

HTMLParamElement.name: HTMLParamElement

name.name: name
name.comment: Sets or retrieves the name of an input parameter for an element.

value.name: value
value.comment: Sets or retrieves the value of an input parameter for an element.

type.name: type
type.comment: Sets or retrieves the content type of the resource designated by the value attribute.

valueType.name: valueType
valueType.comment: Sets or retrieves the data type of the value attribute.

HTMLParamElement.comment: Provides special properties (beyond those of the regular HTMLElement object interface it inherits) for manipulating <param> elements, representing a pair of a key and a value that acts as a parameter for an <object> element.

IntersectionObserver.name: IntersectionObserver
IntersectionObserver.comment: provides a way to asynchronously observe changes in the intersection of a target element with an ancestor element or with a top-level document's viewport.

IntersectionObserverEntry.name: IntersectionObserverEntry
IntersectionObserverEntry.comment: This Intersection Observer API interface describes the intersection between the target element and its root container at a specific moment of transition.

VideoPlaybackQuality.name: VideoPlaybackQuality
VideoPlaybackQuality.comment: Returned by the HTMLVideoElement.getVideoPlaybackQuality() method and contains metrics that can be used to determine the playback quality of a video.

MediaSource.name: MediaSource
MediaSource.comment: This Media Source Extensions API interface represents a source of media data for an HTMLMediaElement object. A MediaSource object can be attached to a HTMLMediaElement to be played in the user agent.

SourceBuffer.name: SourceBuffer
SourceBuffer.comment: A chunk of media to be passed into an HTMLMediaElement and played, via a MediaSource object. This can be made up of one or several media segments.

SourceBufferList.name: SourceBufferList
SourceBufferList.comment: A simple container list for multiple SourceBuffer objects.

MediaStream.name: MediaStream
MediaStream.comment: A stream of media content. A stream consists of several tracks such as video or audio tracks. Each track is specified as an instance of MediaStreamTrack.

MediaStreamTrack.name: MediaStreamTrack
MediaStreamTrack.comment: A single media track within a stream; typically, these are audio or video tracks, but other track types may exist as well.

MediaStreamTrackEvent.name: MediaStreamTrackEvent
MediaStreamTrackEvent.comment: Events which indicate that a MediaStream has had tracks added to or removed from the stream through calls to Media Stream API methods. These events are sent to the stream when these changes occur.

MediaDevices.name: MediaDevices
MediaDevices.comment: Provides access to connected media input devices like cameras and microphones, as well as screen sharing. In essence, it lets you obtain access to any hardware source of media data.

MediaDeviceInfo.name: MediaDeviceInfo
MediaDeviceInfo.comment: The MediaDevicesInfo interface contains information that describes a single media input or output device.

PerformanceNavigationTiming.name: PerformanceNavigationTiming
PerformanceNavigationTiming.comment: Provides methods and properties to store and retrieve metrics regarding the browser's document navigation events. For example, this interface can be used to determine how much time it takes to load or unload a document.

PerformanceTiming.name: PerformanceTiming
PerformanceTiming.deprecated: This interface is deprecated in the Navigation Timing Level 2 specification. Please use the PerformanceNavigationTiming interface instead.
PerformanceTiming.comment: A legacy interface kept for backwards compatibility and contains properties that offer performance timing information for various events which occur during the loading and use of the current page. You get a PerformanceTiming object describing your page using the window.performance.timing property.

PerformanceNavigation.name: PerformanceNavigation
PerformanceNavigation.deprecated: This interface is deprecated in the Navigation Timing Level 2 specification. Please use the PerformanceNavigationTiming interface instead.
PerformanceNavigation.comment: The legacy PerformanceNavigation interface represents information about how the navigation to the current document was done.

Notification.name: Notification
Notification.comment: This Notifications API interface is used to configure and display desktop notifications to the user.

DeviceOrientationEvent.name: DeviceOrientationEvent
DeviceOrientationEvent.comment: The DeviceOrientationEvent provides web developers with information from the physical orientation of the device running the web page.

DeviceMotionEvent.name: DeviceMotionEvent
DeviceMotionEvent.comment: The DeviceMotionEvent provides web developers with information about the speed of changes for the device's position and orientation.

PaymentRequest.name: PaymentRequest
PaymentRequest.comment: This Payment Request API interface is the primary access point into the API, and lets web content and apps accept payments from the end user.

PaymentResponse.name: PaymentResponse
PaymentResponse.comment: This Payment Request API interface is returned after a user selects a payment method and approves a payment request.

PaymentRequestUpdateEvent.name: PaymentRequestUpdateEvent
PaymentRequestUpdateEvent.comment: This Payment Request API interface enables a web page to update the details of a PaymentRequest in response to a user action.

PerformanceEntry.name: PerformanceEntry
PerformanceEntry.comment: Encapsulates a single performance metric that is part of the performance timeline. A performance entry can be directly created by making a performance mark or measure (for example by calling the mark() method) at an explicit point in an application. Performance entries are also created in indirect ways such as loading a resource (such as an image).

PointerEvent.name: PointerEvent
PointerEvent.comment: The state of a DOM event produced by a pointer such as the geometry of the contact point, the device type that generated the event, the amount of pressure that was applied on the contact surface, etc.

PushManager.name: PushManager
PushManager.comment: This Push API interface provides a way to receive notifications from third-party servers as well as request URLs for push notifications.

PushSubscription.name: PushSubscription
PushSubscription.comment: This Push API interface provides a subcription's URL endpoint and allows unsubscription from a push service.

PerformanceResourceTiming.name: PerformanceResourceTiming
PerformanceResourceTiming.comment: Enables retrieval and analysis of detailed network timing data regarding the loading of an application's resources. An application can use the timing metrics to determine, for example, the length of time it takes to fetch a specific resource, such as an XMLHttpRequest, <SVG>, image, or script.

Selection.name: Selection
Selection.comment: A Selection object represents the range of text selected by the user or the current position of the caret. To obtain a Selection object for examination or modification, call Window.getSelection().

ServiceWorker.name: ServiceWorker
ServiceWorker.comment: This ServiceWorker API interface provides a reference to a service worker. Multiple browsing contexts (e.g. pages, workers, etc.) can be associated with the same service worker, each through a unique ServiceWorker object.

ServiceWorkerRegistration.name: ServiceWorkerRegistration
ServiceWorkerRegistration.comment: This ServiceWorker API interface represents the service worker registration. You register a service worker to control one or more pages that share the same origin.

ServiceWorkerContainer.name: ServiceWorkerContainer
ServiceWorkerContainer.comment: The ServiceWorkerContainer interface of the ServiceWorker API provides an object representing the service worker as an overall unit in the network ecosystem, including facilities to register, unregister and update service workers, and access the state of service workers and their registrations.

Cache.name: Cache
Cache.comment: Provides a storage mechanism for Request / Response object pairs that are cached, for example as part of the ServiceWorker life cycle. Note that the Cache interface is exposed to windowed scopes as well as workers. You don't have to use it in conjunction with service workers, even though it is defined in the service worker spec.

SpeechSynthesis.name: SpeechSynthesis
SpeechSynthesis.comment: This Web Speech API interface is the controller interface for the speech service; this can be used to retrieve information about the synthesis voices available on the device, start and pause speech, and other commands besides.

SpeechSynthesisUtterance.name: SpeechSynthesisUtterance
SpeechSynthesisUtterance.comment: This Web Speech API interface represents a speech request. It contains the content the speech service should read and information about how to read it (e.g. language, pitch and volume.)

SpeechSynthesisEvent.name: SpeechSynthesisEvent
SpeechSynthesisEvent.comment: This Web Speech API interface contains information about the current state of SpeechSynthesisUtterance objects that have been processed in the speech service.

SpeechSynthesisVoice.name: SpeechSynthesisVoice
SpeechSynthesisVoice.comment: This Web Speech API interface represents a voice that the system supports. Every SpeechSynthesisVoice has its own relative speech service including information about language, name and URI.

ReadableStream.name: ReadableStream
ReadableStream.comment: This Streams API interface represents a readable stream of byte data. The Fetch API offers a concrete instance of a ReadableStream through the body property of a Response object.

WritableStream.name: WritableStream
WritableStream.comment: This Streams API interface provides a standard abstraction for writing streaming data to a destination, known as a sink. This object comes with built-in backpressure and queuing.

WritableStreamDefaultWriter.name: WritableStreamDefaultWriter
WritableStreamDefaultWriter.comment: This Streams API interface is the object returned by WritableStream.getWriter() and once created locks the < writer to the WritableStream ensuring that no other streams can write to the underlying sink.

WritableStreamDefaultController.name: WritableStreamDefaultController
WritableStreamDefaultController.comment: This Streams API interface represents a controller allowing control of a WritableStream's state. When constructing a WritableStream, the underlying sink is given a corresponding WritableStreamDefaultController instance to manipulate.

ByteLengthQueuingStrategy.name: ByteLengthQueuingStrategy
ByteLengthQueuingStrategy.comment: This Streams API interface provides a built-in byte length queuing strategy that can be used when constructing streams.

CountQueuingStrategy.name: CountQueuingStrategy
CountQueuingStrategy.comment: This Streams API interface provides a built-in byte length queuing strategy that can be used when constructing streams.

Touch.name: Touch
Touch.comment: A single contact point on a touch-sensitive device. The contact point is commonly a finger or stylus and the device may be a touchscreen or trackpad.

TouchList.name: TouchList
TouchList.comment: A list of contact points on a touch surface. For example, if the user has three fingers on the touch surface (such as a screen or trackpad), the corresponding TouchList object would have one Touch object for each finger, for a total of three entries.

TouchEvent.name: TouchEvent
TouchEvent.comment: An event sent when the state of contacts with a touch-sensitive surface changes. This surface can be a touch screen or trackpad, for example. The event can describe one or more points of contact with the screen and includes support for detecting movement, addition and removal of contact points, and so forth.

FocusEvent.name: FocusEvent
FocusEvent.comment: Focus-related events like focus, blur, focusin, or focusout.

MouseEvent.name: MouseEvent

initMouseEvent.name: initMouseEvent
overrideSignatures: initMouseEvent(typeArg: string, canBubbleArg: boolean, cancelableArg: boolean, viewArg: Window, detailArg: number, screenXArg: number, screenYArg: number, clientXArg: number, clientYArg: number, ctrlKeyArg: boolean, altKeyArg: boolean, shiftKeyArg: boolean, metaKeyArg: boolean, buttonArg: number, relatedTargetArg: EventTarget | null): void

MouseEvent.comment: Events that occur due to the user interacting with a pointing device (such as a mouse). Common events using this interface include click, dblclick, mouseup, mousedown.

WheelEvent.name: WheelEvent
WheelEvent.comment: Events that occur due to the user moving a mouse wheel or similar input device.

KeyboardEvent.name: KeyboardEvent
KeyboardEvent.comment: KeyboardEvent objects describe a user interaction with the keyboard; each event describes a single interaction between the user and a key (or combination of a key with modifier keys) on the keyboard.

CompositionEvent.name: CompositionEvent
CompositionEvent.comment: The DOM CompositionEvent represents events that occur due to the user indirectly entering text.

URL.name: URL
URL.comment: The URL interface represents an object providing static methods used for creating object URLs.

append.name: append
append.comment: Appends a specified key/value pair as a new search parameter.

delete.name: delete
delete.comment: Deletes the given search parameter, and its associated value, from the list of all search parameters.

get.name: get
get.comment: Returns the first value associated to the given search parameter.

getAll.name: getAll
getAll.comment: Returns all the values association with a given search parameter.

has.name: has
has.comment: Returns a Boolean indicating if such a search parameter exists.

set.name: set
set.comment: Sets the value associated to a given search parameter to the given value. If there were several values, delete the others.

toString.comment: Returns a string containing a query string suitable for use in a URL. Does not include the question mark.

comment.entries: Returns an array of key, value pairs for every entry in the search params.
comment.keys: Returns a list of keys in the search params.
comment.values: Returns a list of values in the search params.

PerformanceMark.name: PerformanceMark
PerformanceMark.comment: PerformanceMark is an abstract interface for PerformanceEntry objects with an entryType of "mark". Entries of this type are created by calling performance.mark() to add a named DOMHighResTimeStamp (the mark) to the browser's performance timeline.

PerformanceMeasure.name: PerformanceMeasure
PerformanceMeasure.comment: PerformanceMeasure is an abstract interface for PerformanceEntry objects with an entryType of "measure". Entries of this type are created by calling performance.measure() to add a named DOMHighResTimeStamp (the measure) between two marks to the browser's performance timeline.

overrideSignatures: new<T extends ValueType = ValueType>(descriptor: GlobalDescriptor<T>, v?: ValueTypeMap[T]): Global<T>

AudioContext.name: AudioContext
AudioContext.comment: An audio-processing graph built from audio modules linked together, each represented by an AudioNode.

OfflineAudioContext.name: OfflineAudioContext
OfflineAudioContext.comment: An AudioContext interface representing an audio-processing graph built from linked together AudioNodes. In contrast with a standard AudioContext, an OfflineAudioContext doesn't render the audio to the device hardware; instead, it generates it, as fast as it can, and outputs the result to an AudioBuffer.

OfflineAudioCompletionEvent.name: OfflineAudioCompletionEvent
OfflineAudioCompletionEvent.comment: The Web Audio API OfflineAudioCompletionEvent interface represents events that occur when the processing of an OfflineAudioContext is terminated. The complete event implements this interface.

AudioBuffer.name: AudioBuffer
AudioBuffer.comment: A short audio asset residing in memory, created from an audio file using the AudioContext.decodeAudioData() method, or from raw data using AudioContext.createBuffer(). Once put into an AudioBuffer, the audio can then be played by being passed into an AudioBufferSourceNode.

AudioNode.name: AudioNode
AudioNode.comment: A generic interface for representing an audio processing module. Examples include:

AudioParam.name: AudioParam
AudioParam.comment: The Web Audio API's AudioParam interface represents an audio-related parameter, usually a parameter of an AudioNode (such as GainNode.gain).

AnalyserNode.name: AnalyserNode
AnalyserNode.comment: A node able to provide real-time frequency and time-domain analysis information. It is an AudioNode that passes the audio stream unchanged from the input to the output, but allows you to take the generated data, process it, and create audio visualizations.

AudioBufferSourceNode.name: AudioBufferSourceNode
AudioBufferSourceNode.comment: An AudioScheduledSourceNode which represents an audio source consisting of in-memory audio data, stored in an AudioBuffer. It's especially useful for playing back audio which has particularly stringent timing accuracy requirements, such as for sounds that must match a specific rhythm and can be kept in memory rather than being played from disk or the network.

AudioDestinationNode.name: AudioDestinationNode
AudioDestinationNode.comment: AudioDestinationNode has no output (as it is the output, no more AudioNode can be linked after it in the audio graph) and one input. The number of channels in the input must be between 0 and the maxChannelCount value or an exception is raised.

AudioListener.name: AudioListener
AudioListener.comment: The position and orientation of the unique person listening to the audio scene, and is used in audio spatialization. All PannerNodes spatialize in relation to the AudioListener stored in the BaseAudioContext.listener attribute.

AudioProcessingEvent.name: AudioProcessingEvent
AudioProcessingEvent.deprecated: As of the August 29 2014 Web Audio API spec publication, this feature has been marked as deprecated, and is soon to be replaced by AudioWorklet.
AudioProcessingEvent.comment: The Web Audio API events that occur when a ScriptProcessorNode input buffer is ready to be processed.

BiquadFilterNode.name: BiquadFilterNode
BiquadFilterNode.comment: A simple low-order filter, and is created using the AudioContext.createBiquadFilter() method. It is an AudioNode that can represent different kinds of filters, tone control devices, and graphic equalizers.

ChannelMergerNode.name: ChannelMergerNode
ChannelMergerNode.comment: The ChannelMergerNode interface, often used in conjunction with its opposite, ChannelSplitterNode, reunites different mono inputs into a single output. Each input is used to fill a channel of the output. This is useful for accessing each channels separately, e.g. for performing channel mixing where gain must be separately controlled on each channel.

ChannelSplitterNode.name: ChannelSplitterNode
ChannelSplitterNode.comment: The ChannelSplitterNode interface, often used in conjunction with its opposite, ChannelMergerNode, separates the different channels of an audio source into a set of mono outputs. This is useful for accessing each channel separately, e.g. for performing channel mixing where gain must be separately controlled on each channel.

ConvolverNode.name: ConvolverNode
ConvolverNode.comment: An AudioNode that performs a Linear Convolution on a given AudioBuffer, often used to achieve a reverb effect. A ConvolverNode always has exactly one input and one output.

DelayNode.name: DelayNode
DelayNode.comment: A delay-line; an AudioNode audio-processing module that causes a delay between the arrival of an input data and its propagation to the output.

DynamicsCompressorNode.name: DynamicsCompressorNode
DynamicsCompressorNode.comment: Inherits properties from its parent, AudioNode.

GainNode.name: GainNode
GainNode.comment: A change in volume. It is an AudioNode audio-processing module that causes a given gain to be applied to the input data before its propagation to the output. A GainNode always has exactly one input and one output, both with the same number of channels.

IIRFilterNode.name: IIRFilterNode
IIRFilterNode.comment: The IIRFilterNode interface of the Web Audio API is a AudioNode processor which implements a general infinite impulse response (IIR)  filter; this type of filter can be used to implement tone control devices and graphic equalizers as well. It lets the parameters of the filter response be specified, so that it can be tuned as needed.

MediaElementAudioSourceNode.name: MediaElementAudioSourceNode
MediaElementAudioSourceNode.comment: A MediaElementSourceNode has no inputs and exactly one output, and is created using the AudioContext.createMediaElementSource method. The amount of channels in the output equals the number of channels of the audio referenced by the HTMLMediaElement used in the creation of the node, or is 1 if the HTMLMediaElement has no audio.

MediaStreamAudioSourceNode.name: MediaStreamAudioSourceNode
MediaStreamAudioSourceNode.comment: A type of AudioNode which operates as an audio source whose media is received from a MediaStream obtained using the WebRTC or Media Capture and Streams APIs.

OscillatorNode.name: OscillatorNode
OscillatorNode.comment: The OscillatorNode interface represents a periodic waveform, such as a sine wave. It is an AudioScheduledSourceNode audio-processing module that causes a specified frequency of a given wave to be created—in effect, a constant tone.

PannerNode.name: PannerNode
PannerNode.comment: A PannerNode always has exactly one input and one output: the input can be mono or stereo but the output is always stereo (2 channels); you can't have panning effects without at least two audio channels!

PeriodicWave.name: PeriodicWave
PeriodicWave.comment: PeriodicWave has no inputs or outputs; it is used to define custom oscillators when calling OscillatorNode.setPeriodicWave(). The PeriodicWave itself is created/returned by AudioContext.createPeriodicWave().

ScriptProcessorNode.name: ScriptProcessorNode
ScriptProcessorNode.deprecated: As of the August 29 2014 Web Audio API spec publication, this feature has been marked as deprecated, and was replaced by AudioWorklet (see AudioWorkletNode).
ScriptProcessorNode.comment: Allows the generation, processing, or analyzing of audio using JavaScript.

StereoPannerNode.name: StereoPannerNode
StereoPannerNode.comment: The pan property takes a unitless value between -1 (full left pan) and 1 (full right pan). This interface was introduced as a much simpler way to apply a simple panning effect than having to use a full PannerNode.

WaveShaperNode.name: WaveShaperNode
WaveShaperNode.comment: A WaveShaperNode always has exactly one input and one output.

WebGLBuffer.name: WebGLBuffer
WebGLBuffer.comment: Part of the WebGL API and represents an opaque buffer object storing data such as vertices or colors.

WebGLFramebuffer.name: WebGLFramebuffer
WebGLFramebuffer.comment: Part of the WebGL API and represents a collection of buffers that serve as a rendering destination.

WebGLProgram.name: WebGLProgram
WebGLProgram.comment: The WebGLProgram is part of the WebGL API and is a combination of two compiled WebGLShaders consisting of a vertex shader and a fragment shader (both written in GLSL).

WebGLRenderbuffer.name: WebGLRenderbuffer
WebGLRenderbuffer.comment: Part of the WebGL API and represents a buffer that can contain an image, or can be source or target of an rendering operation.

WebGLShader.name: WebGLShader
WebGLShader.comment: The WebGLShader is part of the WebGL API and can either be a vertex or a fragment shader. A WebGLProgram requires both types of shaders.

WebGLTexture.name: WebGLTexture
WebGLTexture.comment: Part of the WebGL API and represents an opaque texture object providing storage and state for texturing operations.

WebGLUniformLocation.name: WebGLUniformLocation
WebGLUniformLocation.comment: Part of the WebGL API and represents the location of a uniform variable in a shader program.

WebGLActiveInfo.name: WebGLActiveInfo
WebGLActiveInfo.comment: Part of the WebGL API and represents the information returned by calling the WebGLRenderingContext.getActiveAttrib() and WebGLRenderingContext.getActiveUniform() methods.

WebGLShaderPrecisionFormat.name: WebGLShaderPrecisionFormat
WebGLShaderPrecisionFormat.comment: Part of the WebGL API and represents the information returned by calling the WebGLRenderingContext.getShaderPrecisionFormat() method.

WebGLRenderingContext.name: WebGLRenderingContext
WebGLRenderingContext.comment: Provides an interface to the OpenGL ES 2.0 graphics rendering context for the drawing surface of an HTML <canvas> element.

WebGLContextEvent.name: WebGLContextEvent
WebGLContextEvent.comment: The WebContextEvent interface is part of the WebGL API and is an interface for an event that is generated in response to a status change to the WebGL rendering context.

DOMException.name: DOMException
DOMException.comment: An abnormal event (called an exception) which occurs as a result of calling a method or accessing a property of a web API.

RTCPeerConnection.name: RTCPeerConnection
RTCPeerConnection.comment: A WebRTC connection between the local computer and a remote peer. It provides methods to connect to a remote peer, maintain and monitor the connection, and close the connection once it's no longer needed.

RTCSessionDescription.name: RTCSessionDescription
RTCSessionDescription.comment: One end of a connection—or potential connection—and how it's configured. Each RTCSessionDescription consists of a description type indicating which part of the offer/answer negotiation process it describes and of the SDP descriptor of the session.

RTCIceCandidate.name: RTCIceCandidate
RTCIceCandidate.comment: The RTCIceCandidate interface—part of the WebRTC API—represents a candidate Internet Connectivity Establishment (ICE) configuration which may be used to establish an RTCPeerConnection.

RTCPeerConnectionIceEvent.name: RTCPeerConnectionIceEvent
RTCPeerConnectionIceEvent.comment: Events that occurs in relation to ICE candidates with the target, usually an RTCPeerConnection. Only one event is of this type: icecandidate.

RTCRtpSender.name: RTCRtpSender
RTCRtpSender.comment: Provides the ability to control and obtain details about how a particular MediaStreamTrack is encoded and sent to a remote peer.

RTCRtpReceiver.name: RTCRtpReceiver
RTCRtpReceiver.comment: This WebRTC API interface manages the reception and decoding of data for a MediaStreamTrack on an RTCPeerConnection.

RTCIceTransport.name: RTCIceTransport
RTCIceTransport.comment: Provides access to information about the ICE transport layer over which the data is being sent and received.

RTCDTMFToneChangeEvent.name: RTCDTMFToneChangeEvent
RTCDTMFToneChangeEvent.comment: Events sent to indicate that DTMF tones have started or finished playing. This interface is used by the tonechange event.

WebSocket.name: WebSocket

close.name: close
close.comment: Closes the WebSocket connection, optionally using code as the the WebSocket connection close code and reason as the the WebSocket connection close reason.

send.name: send
send.comment: Transmits data using the WebSocket connection. data can be a string, a Blob, an ArrayBuffer, or an ArrayBufferView.
overrideSignatures: send(data: string | ArrayBufferLike | Blob | ArrayBufferView): void

url.name: url
url.comment: Returns the URL that was used to establish the WebSocket connection.

readyState.name: readyState
readyState.comment: Returns the state of the WebSocket object's connection. It can have the values described below.

bufferedAmount.name: bufferedAmount
bufferedAmount.comment:
Returns the number of bytes of application data (UTF-8 text and binary data) that have been queued using send() but not yet been transmitted to the network.

If the WebSocket connection is closed, this attribute's value will only increase with each call to the send() method. (The number does not reset to zero once the connection closes.)

extensions.name: extensions
extensions.comment: Returns the extensions selected by the server, if any.

protocol.name: protocol
protocol.comment: Returns the subprotocol selected by the server, if any. It can be used in conjunction with the array form of the constructor's second argument to perform subprotocol negotiation.

binaryType.name: binaryType
binaryType.comment:
Returns a string that indicates how binary data from the WebSocket object is exposed to scripts:

Can be set, to change how binary data is returned. The default is "blob".

WebSocket.comment: Provides the API for creating and managing a WebSocket connection to a server, as well as for sending and receiving data on the connection.

CloseEvent.name: CloseEvent

wasClean.name: wasClean
wasClean.comment: Returns true if the connection closed cleanly; false otherwise.

code.name: code
code.comment: Returns the WebSocket connection close code provided by the server.

reason.name: reason
reason.comment: Returns the WebSocket connection close reason provided by the server.

CloseEvent.comment: A CloseEvent is sent to clients using WebSockets when the connection is closed. This is delivered to the listener indicated by the WebSocket object's onclose attribute.

XMLHttpRequest.name: XMLHttpRequest

open.name: open
open.comment:
Sets the request method, request URL, and synchronous flag.

Throws a "SyntaxError" DOMException if either method is not a valid method or url cannot be parsed.

Throws a "SecurityError" DOMException if method is a case-insensitive match for `CONNECT`, `TRACE`, or `TRACK`.

Throws an "InvalidAccessError" DOMException if async is false, current global object is a Window object, and the timeout attribute is not zero or the responseType attribute is not the empty string.

setRequestHeader.name: setRequestHeader
setRequestHeader.comment:
Combines a header in author request headers.

Throws an "InvalidStateError" DOMException if either state is not opened or the send() flag is set.

Throws a "SyntaxError" DOMException if name is not a header name or if value is not a header value.

send.name: send
send.comment:
Initiates the request. The body argument provides the request body, if any, and is ignored if the request method is GET or HEAD.

Throws an "InvalidStateError" DOMException if either state is not opened or the send() flag is set.

overrideMimeType.name: overrideMimeType
overrideMimeType.comment:
Acts as if the `Content-Type` header value for a response is mime. (It does not change the header.)

Throws an "InvalidStateError" DOMException if state is loading or done.

timeout.name: timeout
timeout.comment:
Can be set to a time in milliseconds. When set to a non-zero value will cause fetching to terminate after the given time has passed. When the time has passed, the request has not yet completed, and this's synchronous flag is unset, a timeout event will then be dispatched, or a "TimeoutError" DOMException will be thrown otherwise (for the send() method).

When set: throws an "InvalidAccessError" DOMException if the synchronous flag is set and current global object is a Window object.

withCredentials.name: withCredentials
withCredentials.comment:
True when credentials are to be included in a cross-origin request. False when they are to be excluded in a cross-origin request and when cookies are to be ignored in its response. Initially false.

When set: throws an "InvalidStateError" DOMException if state is not unsent or opened, or if the send() flag is set.

upload.name: upload
upload.comment: Returns the associated XMLHttpRequestUpload object. It can be used to gather transmission information when data is transferred to a server.

responseType.name: responseType
responseType.comment:
Returns the response type.

Can be set to change the response type. Values are: the empty string (default), "arraybuffer", "blob", "document", "json", and "text".

When set: setting to "document" is ignored if current global object is not a Window object.

When set: throws an "InvalidStateError" DOMException if state is loading or done.

When set: throws an "InvalidAccessError" DOMException if the synchronous flag is set and current global object is a Window object.

responseText.name: responseText
responseText.comment:
Returns response as text.

Throws an "InvalidStateError" DOMException if responseType is not the empty string or "text".

responseXML.name: responseXML
responseXML.comment:
Returns the response as document.

Throws an "InvalidStateError" DOMException if responseType is not the empty string or "document".

XMLHttpRequest.comment: Use XMLHttpRequest (XHR) objects to interact with servers. You can retrieve data from a URL without having to do a full page refresh. This enables a Web page to update just part of a page without disrupting what the user is doing.

FormData.comment: Provides a way to easily construct a set of key/value pairs representing form fields and their values, which can then be easily sent using the XMLHttpRequest.send() method. It uses the same format a form would use if the encoding type were set to "multipart/form-data".

ProgressEvent.name: ProgressEvent
ProgressEvent.comment: Events measuring progress of an underlying process, like an HTTP request (for an XMLHttpRequest, or the loading of the underlying resource of an ,

getElementById.comment: Returns the first element within node's descendants whose ID is elementId.

elementFromPoint.name: elementFromPoint
overrideSignatures: elementFromPoint(x: number, y: number): Element | null

styleSheets.name: styleSheets
styleSheets.comment: Retrieves a collection of styleSheet objects representing the style sheets that correspond to each instance of a link or style object in the document.

activeElement.name: activeElement
activeElement.comment:
Returns the deepest element in the document through which or to which key events are being routed. This is, roughly speaking, the focused element in the document.

For the purposes of this API, when a child browsing context is focused, its container is focused in the parent browsing context. For example, if the user moves the focus to a text control in an iframe, the iframe is the element returned by the activeElement API in the iframe's node document.

Similarly, when the focused element is in a different node tree than documentOrShadowRoot, the element returned will be the host that's located in the same node tree as documentOrShadowRoot if documentOrShadowRoot is a shadow-including inclusive ancestor of the focused element, and null if not.

prepend.name: prepend
prepend.comment:
Inserts nodes before the first child of node, while replacing strings in nodes with equivalent Text nodes.

Throws a "HierarchyRequestError" DOMException if the constraints of the node tree are violated.

append.name: append
append.comment:
Inserts nodes after the last child of node, while replacing strings in nodes with equivalent Text nodes.

Throws a "HierarchyRequestError" DOMException if the constraints of the node tree are violated.

replaceChildren.name: replaceChildren
replaceChildren.comment:
Replace all children of node with nodes, while replacing strings in nodes with equivalent Text nodes.

Throws a "HierarchyRequestError" DOMException if the constraints of the node tree are violated.

querySelector.name: querySelector
querySelector.comment: Returns the first element that is a descendant of node that matches selectors.

querySelectorAll.name: querySelectorAll
querySelectorAll.comment: Returns all element descendants of node that match selectors.

firstElementChild.name: firstElementChild
firstElementChild.comment: Returns the first child that is an element, and null otherwise.

lastElementChild.name: lastElementChild
lastElementChild.comment: Returns the last child that is an element, and null otherwise.

previousElementSibling.name: previousElementSibling
previousElementSibling.comment: Returns the first preceding sibling that is an element, and null otherwise.

nextElementSibling.name: nextElementSibling
nextElementSibling.comment: Returns the first following sibling that is an element, and null otherwise.

before.name: before
before.comment:
Inserts nodes just before node, while replacing strings in nodes with equivalent Text nodes.

Throws a "HierarchyRequestError" DOMException if the constraints of the node tree are violated.

after.name: after
after.comment:
Inserts nodes just after node, while replacing strings in nodes with equivalent Text nodes.

Throws a "HierarchyRequestError" DOMException if the constraints of the node tree are violated.

replaceWith.name: replaceWith
replaceWith.comment:
Replaces node with nodes, while replacing strings in nodes with equivalent Text nodes.

Throws a "HierarchyRequestError" DOMException if the constraints of the node tree are violated.

fatal.name: fatal
fatal.comment: Returns true if error mode is "fatal", otherwise false.

ignoreBOM.name: ignoreBOM
ignoreBOM.comment: Returns the value of ignore BOM.

href.name: href
href.comment:
Returns the hyperlink's URL.

Can be set, to change the URL.

protocol.name: protocol
protocol.comment:
Returns the hyperlink's URL's scheme.

Can be set, to change the URL's scheme.

username.name: username
username.comment:
Returns the hyperlink's URL's username.

Can be set, to change the URL's username.

password.name: password
password.comment:
Returns the hyperlink's URL's password.

Can be set, to change the URL's password.

host.name: host
host.comment:
Returns the hyperlink's URL's host and port (if different from the default port for the scheme).

Can be set, to change the URL's host and port.

hostname.name: hostname
hostname.comment:
Returns the hyperlink's URL's host.

Can be set, to change the URL's host.

port.name: port
port.comment:
Returns the hyperlink's URL's port.

Can be set, to change the URL's port.

pathname.name: pathname
pathname.comment:
Returns the hyperlink's URL's path.

Can be set, to change the URL's path.

search.name: search
search.comment:
Returns the hyperlink's URL's query (includes leading "?" if non-empty).

Can be set, to change the URL's query (ignores leading "?").

hash.name: hash
hash.comment:
Returns the hyperlink's URL's fragment (includes leading "#" if non-empty).

Can be set, to change the URL's fragment (ignores leading "#").

Fires when the user aborts the download.
@param ev The event.

onblur.name: onblur
onblur.comment:
Fires when the object loses the input focus.
@param ev The focus event.

oncanplay.name: oncanplay
oncanplay.comment:
Occurs when playback is possible, but would require further buffering.
@param ev The event.

onchange.name: onchange
onchange.comment:
Fires when the contents of the object or selection have changed.
@param ev The event.

onclick.name: onclick
onclick.comment:
Fires when the user clicks the left mouse button on the object
@param ev The mouse event.

oncontextmenu.name: oncontextmenu
oncontextmenu.comment:
Fires when the user clicks the right mouse button in the client area, opening the context menu.
@param ev The mouse event.

ondblclick.name: ondblclick
ondblclick.comment:
Fires when the user double-clicks the object.
@param ev The mouse event.

ondrag.name: ondrag
ondrag.comment:
Fires on the source object continuously during a drag operation.
@param ev The event.

ondragend.name: ondragend
ondragend.comment:
Fires on the source object when the user releases the mouse at the close of a drag operation.
@param ev The event.

ondragenter.name: ondragenter
ondragenter.comment:
Fires on the target element when the user drags the object to a valid drop target.
@param ev The drag event.

ondragleave.name: ondragleave
ondragleave.comment:
Fires on the target object when the user moves the mouse out of a valid drop target during a drag operation.
@param ev The drag event.

ondragover.name: ondragover
ondragover.comment:
Fires on the target element continuously while the user drags the object over a valid drop target.
@param ev The event.

ondragstart.name: ondragstart
ondragstart.comment:
Fires on the source object when the user starts to drag a text selection or selected object.
@param ev The event.

ondurationchange.name: ondurationchange
ondurationchange.comment:
Occurs when the duration attribute is updated.
@param ev The event.

onemptied.name: onemptied
onemptied.comment:
Occurs when the media element is reset to its initial state.
@param ev The event.

onended.name: onended
onended.comment:
Occurs when the end of playback is reached.
@param ev The event

onerror.name: onerror
onerror.comment:
Fires when an error occurs during object loading.
@param ev The event.

onfocus.name: onfocus
onfocus.comment:
Fires when the object receives focus.
@param ev The event.

onkeydown.name: onkeydown
onkeydown.comment:
Fires when the user presses a key.
@param ev The keyboard event

onkeypress.name: onkeypress
onkeypress.comment:
Fires when the user presses an alphanumeric key.
@param ev The event.

onkeyup.name: onkeyup
onkeyup.comment:
Fires when the user releases a key.
@param ev The keyboard event

onload.name: onload
onload.comment:
Fires immediately after the browser loads the object.
@param ev The event.

onloadeddata.name: onloadeddata
onloadeddata.comment:

onloadedmetadata.name: onloadedmetadata
onloadedmetadata.comment:
Occurs when the duration and dimensions of the media have been determined.
@param ev The event.

onloadstart.name: onloadstart
onloadstart.comment:
Occurs when Internet Explorer begins looking for media data.

onmousedown.name: onmousedown

onmousemove.name: onmousemove

onmouseout.name: onmouseout

Fires when the user moves the mouse pointer outside the boundaries of the object.

onmouseover.name: onmouseover
onmouseover.comment:

onmouseup.name: onmouseup

onpause.name: onpause

onplay.name: onplay

onplaying.name: onplaying

onprogress.name: onprogress

onratechange.name: onratechange

onreset.name: onreset
onreset.comment:

onscroll.name: onscroll
onscroll.comment:

onseeked.name: onseeked
onseeked.comment:
Occurs when the seek operation ends.

onseeking.name: onseeking
onseeking.comment:

onselect.comment:

onsuspend.name: onsuspend

ontimeupdate.name: ontimeupdate

onvolumechange.name: onvolumechange
